author: claude
desc: Separate the two things ticket 221 conflated. Round 11 concluded the gP13/gP19 SMC key writes break 14-core boot because removing pwren-gpios fixed it -- but pwren-gpios ALSO powers the PCIe endpoints, so removing it stops brcmfmac, hci_bcm4377 and sdhci-pci probing and removes all their DMA. Verified: every DTB that boots 14 cores has pwren-gpios count 0; the only one that hangs has 2. So the sound statement is only that something in the chain SMC-key-write -> endpoint-power -> driver-probe -> endpoint-DMA breaks the boot. TEST: keep pwren-gpios (SMC write happens, endpoints power up) but build WITHOUT the endpoint drivers -- disable BRCMFMAC, BT_HCIBCM4377, MMC_SDHCI_PCI. 14 cores boot => SMC write and power-up innocent, an endpoint driver's DMA is the culprit; bisect one at a time, brcmfmac first (large firmware DMA through the DART). Still hangs => drivers innocent and round 11's SMC-write conclusion is restored on sound evidence. ALSO: the macOS GPIO value 0x00800001 (vs CMD_OUTPUT|1) was tested at 14 cores and does NOT fix the hang -- refuted, experiment reverted. AND get DOCKCHANNEL_EARLYCON output: the 14-core hang is still pass/fail with zero diagnosis, which is the main thing slowing this down. RESULT 2026-08-03 (valid re-run): lease live, maxcpus=14 asserted from dcuart-boot.log, logs deleted before each boot. CONTROL endpoint drivers ON = hang (20 lines). EXPERIMENT endpoint drivers OFF (BRCMFMAC/BT_HCIBCM4377/MMC_SDHCI_PCI disabled, kbuild-asserted) with pwren-gpios still present = ALSO hang (20 lines). So ENDPOINT DRIVERS ARE EXONERATED -- their DMA is not the cause, and round 11s conclusion is restored: the trigger is the gP13/gP19 SMC key write and the port power-up it performs. CRITICAL PROCESS NOTE: the rig lease (1 h) expired during round 12 and rig-guard refused every boot; because the boot script was invoked with >/dev/null the refusal was invisible and STALE logs were read as results (identical 535-line counts, maxcpus=1 regardless of what was passed). INVALIDATED and needing re-run: the macOS GPIO value test at 14 cores, the first 223 run, and BOTH earlycon attempts -- the claim "the kernel dies before earlycon initialises" is WITHDRAWN. New standing rules: never suppress rig-script output; delete the log before each boot and treat a short log as "boot did not happen"; assert the cmdline from dcuart-boot.log every run; renew the lease per batch. ROUND 14 2026-08-03: macOS GPIO value re-tested under VALID methodology (lease renewed, logs deleted per boot, maxcpus=14 asserted from dcuart-boot.log, output not suppressed, endpoint drivers enabled, TWO runs): both HANG. So writing macOS 0x00800001 instead of CMD_OUTPUT|1 does NOT fix the 14-core hang -- the refutation now stands on real evidence, and gpio-macsmc should NOT be changed on the strength of sol decode (which is itself correct; the values do differ, it is just not the cause). Experiment reverted, known-good kernel rebuilt, 1-core SD-root desktop verified back up. NEXT HIGHEST VALUE: real diagnostics for the 14-core hang -- it is still pass/fail with zero visibility. Options: earlycon=dockchannel with the CORRECT data-window address taken from the DT (not a guess); m1n1-side tracing of the SMC key write; or bisect WHICH key (gP13 WiFi vs gP19 SD) triggers it, which is cheap and might permit WiFi at full core count before the mechanism is understood.
